about: Speaking сдают вдвоём с другим кандидатом, длится около 14 минут. В комнате два экзаменатора: один задаёт вопросы, второй только слушает и ставит оценки.

Оценивают 4 критерия: Grammar & Vocabulary (точность и разнообразие), Discourse Management (связно ли и достаточно ли длинно ты говоришь), Pronunciation (понятно ли тебя), Interactive Communication (как ты общаешься с партнёром).
Главное правило: отвечай развёрнуто. Ответ + причина + пример — и ты уже звучишь на B2. Одно слово «Yes» — почти ноль баллов.
Не учи готовые ответы наизусть: экзаменаторы это слышат. Учи фразы-связки — они подходят к любому вопросу.

general.note: Те самые «слова-паразиты», только правильные. Дают 2–3 секунды подумать и звучат естественно. Не больше одной на ответ и не начинай каждый ответ с Well.
p: I've never really thought about it, but…
Никогда об этом не задумывался, но…
Off the top of my head, …

general.note: Чередуй, не повторяй I think в каждом предложении.
p: I'm not entirely sure, but I'd guess…
Я не совсем уверен, но предположу…

general.note: Каждое мнение — с причиной. Это самый простой способ сделать ответ длиннее.

p: И не только это, но и…

general.t: Не понял вопрос или забыл слово
general.note: Переспросить — нормально, за это не снижают. Молчать — плохо.
p: Sorry, could you repeat the question, please?
Sorry, I didn't quite catch that.
I can't remember the word, but it's a kind of…
Не помню слово, но это такой вид…
Let me put it another way.
At the end of the day, …

parts.name: Interview
parts.what: Экзаменатор задаёт каждому кандидату по очереди простые вопросы о нём самом: дом, учёба или работа, свободное время, путешествия, планы.
parts.check: Можешь ли ты легко говорить о себе: понятно, без долгих пауз и чуть подробнее, чем одним предложением.
tips: Ответ на 20–30 секунд: 2–4 предложения. Не одно слово, но и не монолог на минуту.
Показывай разные времена: I used to…, I've been…, I'm planning to…
Улыбайся и смотри на экзаменатора — это просто разговор.
mistakes: Повторять вопрос целиком: Do I live in a house or a flat? I live in a flat.
Рассказывать заученный текст не по вопросу.

p: Whenever I get the chance, I…
I'm not a big fan of…
I'm planning to… / I'm hoping to…

questions.q: Do you live in a house or a flat?
questions.a: I live in a flat with my parents and my younger sister. [[To be honest]], it's not very big, but it's in a really convenient area — there's a metro station just five minutes away. [[I'd love to]] live in a house with a garden [[one day]], though.

questions.q: What do you like most about your neighbourhood?
questions.a: [[Well]], the best thing is probably the park near my building. [[Whenever I get the chance]], I go running there in the morning. [[What's more]], there are lots of small cafés, so it's a great place to meet friends.

questions.q: What do you enjoy doing at the weekend?
questions.a: [[It depends on]] the weather, [[actually]]. If it's sunny, I [[usually]] go cycling with my friends. If it's cold, [[I'd rather]] stay at home and watch a series [[than]] go out. Last weekend, for example, I watched four episodes in one evening!

questions.q: Do you prefer spending time indoors or outdoors?
questions.a: Definitely outdoors. [[The main reason is that]] I spend the whole week sitting at a desk, so at the weekend I need some fresh air. [[Having said that]], in winter I [[tend to]] stay inside more.

questions.q: What do you enjoy most about your studies?
questions.a: [[I'm really into]] languages, so English lessons are my favourite. [[That's because]] our teacher makes them really interactive — we do debates and projects instead of just grammar exercises.

questions.q: Is there anything you would like to learn in the future?
questions.a: Yes, [[I'm hoping to]] learn how to play the guitar. I [[used to]] play the piano when I was a child, [[but]] I gave up. [[I firmly believe that]] it's never too late to start again.

questions.q: Do you spend a lot of time with your family?
questions.a: Not as much as I'd like, [[to be honest]]. During the week everyone is busy, [[but]] on Sundays we always have lunch together. It's kind of a family tradition.

questions.q: Tell us about your best friend.
questions.a: My best friend is called Anna. We've known each other since primary school, so almost ten years now. What I like most about her is that she's really honest — she always tells me the truth, even when I don't want to hear it.

questions.q: Where did you go on your last holiday?
questions.a: Last summer I went to the seaside with my family. We spent two weeks there, and [[to be honest]], it was the best holiday I've ever had. We swam every day and even tried diving for the first time.

questions.q: Would you rather travel alone or with friends?
questions.a: With friends, definitely. [[That's because]] it's much more fun to share experiences with people you know. [[On the other hand]], I can see why some people travel alone — you can do exactly what you want.

questions.q: How much time do you spend on your phone every day?
questions.a: [[Honestly]], probably too much — about four or five hours. Most of the time I'm chatting with friends or watching videos. I'm trying to cut down, [[though]], because it's quite distracting when I'm studying.

questions.q: Do you enjoy cooking?
questions.a: [[I'm not a big fan of]] cooking every day, [[but]] I like making something special at the weekend. Last Saturday, [[for example]], I made pizza from scratch, and it turned out really well!

questions.q: What would you like to be doing in five years' time?
questions.a: [[That's a tricky one]]. [[I'd say]] I'd like to be studying at university, ideally abroad. [[I'm planning to]] apply to a programme in computer science, so I'm working hard on my English right now.

questions.q: Are you a morning person?
questions.a: Not at all! [[I can't stand]] getting up early. [[Having said that]], I've noticed that I study much better in the morning, so I'm trying to change my habits.

parts.name: Long turn
parts.what: Тебе дают две фотографии и вопрос над ними. Ты говоришь 1 минуту: сравниваешь фото и отвечаешь на вопрос. Потом партнёру задают короткий вопрос про твои фото (~30 секунд). Затем вы меняетесь.
parts.check: Умеешь ли ты сравнивать, предполагать (might, could, looks as if) и говорить целую минуту связно, без длинных пауз.
tips: Не описывай каждую деталь. Задача — сравнить и ответить на вопрос.
Примерно 20 секунд на сравнение и 40 секунд на вопрос над фото.
Предполагай: They might be…, It looks as if…, They must be… — ты же не знаешь наверняка.
Слушай партнёра, пока он говорит про свои фото: тебе потом зададут вопрос.
mistakes: «In the first picture I can see a man. He has a blue T-shirt…» — описание вместо сравнения.
Забыть вопрос над фотографиями и проговорить всю минуту о другом.
Остановиться через 30 секунд. Если мысли кончились — добавь, что выбрал бы ты сам.

p: In the first picture…, whereas in the second…
На первой фотографии…, тогда как на второй…
Одно большое различие в том, что…
Unlike the people in the first photo, …
В отличие от людей на первом фото, …
Я бы предпочёл…, в основном потому что…
For me, it would have to be…

questions.q: Compare the photographs and say what the advantages of learning in these different ways might be.
questions.q2: Which way of learning would you prefer? Why?
questions.a: [[Both pictures show]] people learning, but in very different ways. [[In the first picture]], there's a group of students in a classroom with a teacher, [[whereas in the second]] a young man is studying alone at home on his laptop. [[It looks as if]] the students in the classroom are enjoying the lesson — [[they seem to be]] paying attention and asking questions. The main advantage of learning like this is that you can get help from the teacher immediately and learn from your classmates. [[On the other hand]], the man in the second photo can study whenever he wants and at his own speed. [[He might be]] working during the day, so online learning is probably more convenient for him. [[Having said that]], it must be quite hard to stay motivated without anyone around. [[So, all in all]], [[I'd say]] both ways have clear advantages.

questions.q: Compare the photographs and say why people might choose to spend their free time in these places.
questions.q2: Which of these places would you like to spend a day in? Why?
questions.a: [[Both pictures show]] people relaxing in their free time, but the atmosphere is completely different. [[In the first picture]], a family is having a picnic in a quiet park, [[whereas in the second]] there's a huge crowd at an outdoor music festival. [[I'd imagine that]] the family chose the park because it's peaceful and they can spend time together without any distractions. [[They might also]] want to save money. [[Unlike the people in the first photo]], the people at the festival are looking for excitement. [[Judging by their faces]], they're having an amazing time — [[they must be]] fans of the band. A festival is a great way to meet new people and see your favourite artists live. [[However]], it can be very noisy and tiring. [[Overall, I'd say]] it depends on whether you want to relax or have fun.

questions.q: Compare the photographs and say what people might enjoy about these different kinds of holidays.
questions.q2: Which kind of holiday do you prefer? Why?
questions.a: [[In the first picture]], two friends are hiking in the mountains, [[whereas in the second]] a couple is relaxing by the sea. [[One big difference is that]] the first holiday is quite active, while the second one looks very calm. The hikers [[might be]] enjoying the challenge of reaching the top and the amazing views. [[They seem to be]] tired, but happy. [[What's more]], this kind of holiday is usually cheaper. [[On the other hand]], the couple on the beach [[must be]] enjoying the sunshine and doing absolutely nothing. [[I'd imagine that]] they have stressful jobs, so they just want to rest. [[Personally, I'd say]] both holidays sound great, but for different reasons.

questions.q: Compare the photographs and say why people might choose to eat in these different ways.
questions.q2: Do you prefer eating at home or in a restaurant? Why?
questions.a: [[Both pictures show]] people having a meal together. [[In the first picture]], a family is cooking at home, [[whereas in the second]] a group of friends is eating in a restaurant. [[It looks as if]] the family is having a lot of fun — even the child is helping. People might choose to cook at home because it's healthier and much cheaper. [[Apart from that]], cooking together can bring a family closer. [[Unlike the family in the first photo]], the friends in the restaurant don't have to do any work. [[They might be]] celebrating something, like a birthday. Eating out is more convenient and you can try dishes you can't make yourself. [[However]], it can be quite expensive. [[So, all in all]], I think it depends on the occasion.

parts.name: Collaborative task
parts.what: Вам с партнёром дают вопрос и 5 вариантов (mind map). 2 минуты вы обсуждаете варианты друг с другом, потом экзаменатор задаёт второй вопрос — и у вас 1 минута, чтобы прийти к решению.
parts.check: Умеешь ли ты общаться: начинать разговор, спрашивать мнение партнёра, реагировать на его слова, вежливо не соглашаться и договариваться.
tips: Говори с партнёром, а не с экзаменатором. Смотри на него.
Не надо обсудить все 5 вариантов — важнее хорошо поговорить о 3–4.
Реагируй на слова партнёра, а потом добавляй своё: That's a good point, and also…
Не принимай решение в первые 2 минуты — его спросят отдельно.
Не обязательно соглашаться. Можно и не договориться — главное, обсуждать.
mistakes: Говорить монологом минуту, не давая партнёру слова.
Игнорировать, что сказал партнёр, и говорить своё.
Решить за 20 секунд «Let's choose sport» — и замолчать.

p: А как ты на это смотришь?
I see what you mean, but…
I'm not so sure about that.
Я не так уверен в этом.
That's true to some extent, but…
So, which one shall we choose?

questions.q: Here are some things that can help people stay healthy. Talk to each other about how these things can help people stay healthy.
questions.q2: Which two things are the most important for young people?
a: A
[[Shall we start with]] doing sport? [[I firmly believe that]] it's the most obvious way to stay healthy.
B
[[I couldn't agree more]]. It keeps you fit, and [[what's more]], it's good for your mood. [[How do you feel about]] eating fresh food?
A
It's important, of course, but it can be quite expensive. Fresh fruit and vegetables cost a lot nowadays.
B
[[I see what you mean, but]] cooking at home is still cheaper than fast food. [[What about this one]] — getting enough sleep?
A
[[That's a good point]]. Lots of teenagers stay up late on their phones, so they're tired all day.
B
[[Exactly!]] And that's connected to screen time. [[If you ask me]], less screen time would help people sleep better.
A
True. [[Shall we move on to]] spending time with friends? It's more about mental health, [[would you agree]]?
B
Yes, definitely. Feeling lonely can be just as bad as not exercising.
a2: [[So, which one shall we choose]]? I'd say sport and sleep.
[[I'm not so sure about]] sport. [[It seems we both think]] sleep is really important, but I'd go for less screen time as well, because it affects everything else.
[[I take your point]]. OK, [[shall we go for]] sleep and less screen time?
Yes, let's go for those two.
questions.c: How can these things help people stay healthy?

questions.q: Here are some skills that young people could learn before they leave school. Talk to each other about why these skills might be useful.
questions.q2: Which skill do you think is the most useful?
a: A
[[Shall I go first]]? I think managing money is really useful. Lots of young people have no idea how to plan a budget.
B
[[That's a good point]]. When you start university and live alone, you suddenly have to pay for everything. [[What do you think]] about cooking?
A
It's connected, [[actually]]. If you can cook, you save a lot of money.
B
[[Absolutely]]. [[What about this one]] — first aid? [[I'd imagine that]] it could even save someone's life.
A
[[That's true to some extent, but]] you probably won't need it very often. Speaking a foreign language, [[on the other hand]], is useful every day.
B
[[I see what you mean]]. It opens up so many opportunities — for travel, for jobs. And public speaking?
A
[[To be honest]], I'm terrified of it! [[But]] that's exactly why it should be taught at school.
a2: [[So, which one shall we choose]]? For me, it would have to be a foreign language.
[[I'm not so sure about that]]. Managing money affects everybody, but not everyone needs a foreign language.
[[I take your point]], but in today's world almost every job needs English.
questions.c: Why might these skills be useful for young people?

questions.q: Here are some ways a town could be made better for young people. Talk to each other about how these things could improve a town for young people.
questions.q2: Which idea would make the biggest difference?
a: A
[[Let's begin with]] the sports centre. It would give young people somewhere to go after school.
B
[[Exactly]]. [[Not only that, but]] it would keep them active. [[How do you feel about]] cycle lanes?
A
In my town, cycling is quite dangerous because of the traffic, so more cycle lanes would be great.
B
[[I couldn't agree more]]. And cheaper public transport would help too — young people don't usually have cars.
A
[[That's a good point]]. [[What's your take on]] a music venue?
B
[[Honestly]], I think it would be popular, [[but]] maybe only with a small group of people. Parks are for everyone.
A
True, although most towns already have a few parks.
a2: [[So, which one shall we choose]]? I'd go for cheaper public transport.
[[The main reason is that]] it helps young people get to everything else — the sports centre, concerts, school.
[[That's a good point]]. [[Shall we go for]] public transport, then?
questions.c: How could these things improve a town for young people?

questions.q: Here are some areas of life that technology has changed. Talk to each other about how technology has changed these areas of people's lives.
questions.q2: In which area has technology had the most positive effect?
a: A
[[Shall we start with]] shopping? Nowadays you can buy almost anything online without leaving your house.
B
[[Absolutely]]. [[Having said that]], I think some people miss going to real shops. [[What do you think]] about friendships?
A
[[That's a tricky one]]. On the one hand, you can stay in touch with friends who live far away.
B
[[I see what you mean, but]] people spend less time together face to face. [[What about]] studying?
A
There it's definitely positive. You can find information on anything in seconds, and there are lots of online courses.
B
[[I couldn't agree more]]. And work has changed too — lots of people work from home now.
A
True, although some people find it hard to stop working in the evening.
a2: [[So, which one shall we choose]]? [[I'd say]] studying.
[[It seems we both think]] studying has changed the most. I agree it's been mostly positive.
Great, [[shall we go for]] studying, then?
questions.c: How has technology changed these areas of people's lives?

parts.name: Discussion
parts.what: Экзаменатор задаёт вопросы, связанные с темой Part 3, — уже более общие и абстрактные. Можно отвечать самому и добавлять к ответу партнёра.
parts.check: Можешь ли ты развить мнение: объяснить, привести пример, посмотреть с двух сторон. Это самая «взрослая» часть.
tips: Ответ на 30–45 секунд: мнение → причина → пример → другая сторона.
Если вопрос задали партнёру, можно добавить: Can I just add something?
Нет мнения? Не говори «I don't know» — скажи I've never really thought about it, but… и порассуждай.
Говори о людях в целом, а не только о себе: Generally speaking, young people…
mistakes: Ответ в одно предложение без причины.
Перебивать партнёра или полностью молчать, когда говорит он.

p: On the one hand…, on the other hand…
С одной стороны…, с другой стороны…
In the future, it's likely that…
Я бы не удивился, если бы…
I agree with what … said about…
Я согласен с тем, что … сказал про…
Going back to what you said, …
Возвращаясь к тому, что ты сказал, …

questions.q: Do you think schools should do more to help students stay healthy?
questions.a: Yes, [[I firmly believe that]] they should. [[The main reason is that]] students spend most of their day at school, so it has a huge influence on their habits. [[For example]], schools could offer healthier food in the canteen or more PE lessons. [[Having said that]], [[I'd say]] parents are just as responsible — schools can't do everything.

questions.q: Why do you think some people find it difficult to exercise regularly?
questions.a: [[Generally speaking]], I think it's mainly about time. People work long hours, and when they get home, they're exhausted. [[What's more]], gyms can be quite expensive. [[On the other hand]], you don't really need a gym — you can go running for free. [[So]] maybe it's also about motivation.

questions.q: Is it better to learn practical skills at school or at home?
questions.a: [[That's a tricky one]]. [[On the one hand]], parents can teach things like cooking in a more relaxed way. [[On the other hand]], not all parents have the time or the skills. [[That's why I think]] schools should at least teach the basics, so that everyone has the same chance.

questions.q: Some people say that young people today have fewer practical skills than in the past. Do you agree?
questions.a: [[To some extent]], yes. My grandparents can fix almost anything, while I'd just look for a video online! [[However]], young people have other skills — [[for instance]], we're much better with technology. [[So, all in all]], [[I'd say]] the skills have changed rather than disappeared.

questions.q: Would you prefer to live in a big city or a small town in the future?
questions.a: [[Personally, I'd say]] a big city, at least while I'm young. [[That's because]] there are more opportunities for work and study, and there's always something to do. [[Having said that]], I can imagine moving to a small town when I'm older, because life there is calmer and cheaper.

questions.q: Who should be responsible for making towns better for young people — the government or young people themselves?
questions.a: [[I think]] it should be both. The government has the money, so it should pay for things like sports centres and transport. [[But]] young people should also be involved, because they know best what they need. [[For example]], in some towns teenagers can vote on how part of the budget is spent, which [[I'd say]] is a great idea.

questions.q: Do you think people will still read printed books in the future?
questions.a: [[I'm not entirely sure, but I'd guess]] yes. Lots of people, including me, still love the feeling of a real book. [[However]], [[I wouldn't be surprised if]] printed books became more of a luxury, like vinyl records. [[In most cases]], people will probably read on screens.

questions.q: Some people say we rely too much on technology. What do you think?
questions.a: [[I'd agree to some extent]]. [[Take]] navigation [[for example]] — hardly anyone can read a paper map anymore. If the internet stopped working for a day, [[I think people would]] panic! [[On the other hand]], technology makes our lives so much easier. [[It's a double-edged sword]], really.

questions.q: Do you think young people have enough free time nowadays?
questions.a: [[Honestly]], I don't think so. Between school, homework and extra classes, many teenagers are busy from morning till night. [[What's more]], they often feel they have to be productive all the time. [[I firmly believe that]] free time is important — it's when you actually rest and become creative.

questions.q: Is it important for young people to travel to other countries?
questions.a: Yes, [[I'd say]] it's really valuable. [[That's because]] travelling helps you understand other cultures and become more independent. [[For example]], when I went abroad for the first time, I had to speak English in real situations, which boosted my confidence. [[However]], [[it depends on]] money — not everyone can afford it.
